en: “Having formerly been a sovereign monarch, enjoying unsurpassed and abundant sensual pleasures...”
Thus now, cast into this difficult hell,
he did not lose his former beauty and strength.
"Even before, patience and austerity were mine..."
Once established, it became difficult to overcome;
now that I have obtained it, O King,
how could I abandon my former beauty and strength?
It is said that all these [tasks] were thus completed by the illustrious and wise one who was capable;
having attained former and sublime renown, he—
Do not abandon your former luster and strength.
O Lord of Men, having cast away happiness with suffering, or suffering with happiness, endure that which is difficult to bear.
“Being at peace in both states because they have attained final liberation,
they remain the same in both happiness and suffering.
Thus ends the Third Jātaka, the Ekarāja-jātaka.
